name: Tony Allen
hook: The drummer Fela Kuti said Afrobeat could not exist without, who left Fela in 1979 and spent the next forty years teaching the beat to musicians from Paris to London.
blurb: Tony Allen was born in Lagos in 1940. He was the drummer and musical director of Fela Kuti's band Africa 70 from 1968 to 1979, and the two of them invented Afrobeat. Allen created its drum language, which spreads separate patterns across the kick, snare, hi-hat and toms so the kit plays several rhythms at once. Fela's remark that without Tony Allen there would be no Afrobeat is widely reported, and Brian Eno has called him perhaps the greatest drummer who has ever lived. Allen left in 1979, unhappy about royalties, credit and the band's finances. In 2000 Blur sang about him in 'Music Is My Radar', and he got in touch with Damon Albarn. They made music together for the rest of his life, including in The Good, the Bad & the Queen (2007). He died in Paris in 2020.
